observation.visible_scene: First-person view from an orange sea kayak floating on dark, choppy water with patches of white foam, beside a large rocky cliff/headland on the right under a flat overcast sky. A black 'Werner' paddle blade is held up on the left side at the start of the clip.
visible_changes: The paddle blade begins raised in the upper-left, then travels downward and exits the frame over roughly the first 0.3–0.4 s, stays out of view for a long interval, re-enters as a small black edge at the lower-left corner around 1.1–1.3 s, and then leaves again.
The orange kayak bow remains near the bottom center/right throughout, bobbing vertically relative to the frame as the camera rises and falls with the swell.

The background drifts and tilts slightly: the cliff shifts position at the right edge and the horizon line rocks, indicating the kayak/camera is yawing and rolling rather than the cliff itself moving.
Foreground whitewater patches continuously reshape and redistribute, and the dark swell line in the mid-distance appears to steepen/rise somewhat across the excerpt.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the paddle's re-entry corresponds to a stroke, a rest, or a brace, and what the paddler does after the clip ends.
The kayak's actual direction of travel relative to the cliff (paddling along it, toward it, or holding position).
Whether the mid-distance wave is genuinely growing or the camera is simply moving up its face.
Any motion or actions before t=0 or after the last frame.
uncertain_details: Exact cause of the horizon tilt (camera roll vs. wave-induced pitch).
Whether the small black shape at the lower-left in later frames is the same paddle blade or a different part of the gear.
Precise magnitude of the swell's change versus camera bobbing.
